pages.text: "Seaweed soup!" Dari hopped to the kitchen table. Shellfish and seaweed soup steamed as the first snow fell outside. He gripped his spoon in his mouth. "Quickly, then out to see the snow!"
Dari slurped big spoonfuls without chewing. Gulp, gulp! Whole shellfish pieces went down, too. "Quickly for the snow!" Soon the bowl was half empty.
Suddenly—"Hic! Hic!" His tummy felt hard as a stone and ached. Dari dropped the spoon and held his tummy, flattening against the table. "Mom... it hurts..."
Mom quickly stroked his back. "You swallowed too fast. The doctor's coming today." Kkiruk called from the roof, "A boat!" Mom opened the kitchen door.
A sea turtle doctor with a big bag came in, brushing off snow. The doctor gently pressed Dari's tummy. "Swallowed without chewing? All clogged up inside." A sip of warm water settled his hiccups.
"Even without teeth, I work food slowly in my mouth. Watch." The doctor took a little soup. One, two, three... ten, then swallow! "Eat-like-a-turtle game. Chew well, take your time!" Dari perked up.
Dari took a small spoonful. Chew, chew—one, two, three... ten! The seaweed grew soft and the shellfish sweet. "Was it always this good?" Chew well, take your time!
The bowl emptied. His tummy felt soft and comfortable. "No hiccups! No ache!" Dari slapped his tail. Smiling, the doctor closed the bag.
Now Dari knew the steps. "One, a little on my spoon! Two, ten chews! Three, swallow when it's chewed!" Next dinner, he ate slowly like a turtle again.
Mom hugged him by the window. "A fine Dari who chews well! Let's see the snow!" Slow chewing made food tastier and his tummy comfortable. "Chew well, take your time!" Snow piled outside as he smiled.
